identity_rationale: Giorgio Agamben, born 1942, identified through the European Graduate School biography’s concordant Homo sacer (1995) and Stato di eccezione (2003), and the named 2004 Raulff interview about those works. New curated identity giorgio_agamben; no authority ID guessed, automatic crosswalk or namesake merger.

screening.role: Selection context only, not substantive proof or automatic identity resolution.

sources.title: Ulrich Raulff, An Interview with Giorgio Agamben, German Law Journal 5.5 (2004): 609–614; Morag Goodwin translation
sources.note: Complete interview pp. 609–614 including editorial notes read. Conversation Rome 4 March 2004; German Süddeutsche Zeitung publication 6 April; English translation Morag Goodwin. Agamben explicitly distinguishes paradigmatic method from being a historian and names Foucault’s panopticon/archaeology as resources. Editor notes are distinct from answers. Incidental 1968 Collège course and 1934 Nuremberg-law dates are erroneous and not adopted; policy/historical generalizations are attributed, not independently established. Books unread.

substantive_relations.relationship: Uses the state of exception as a paradigm for examining the relation of law, anomy and governmental power.
substantive_relations.note: Own interview pp. 609–612 read. The emergency-to-normal-government thesis is attributed to Agamben; this is a philosophical paradigm rather than independent verification of an encompassing history of states.

substantive_relations.relationship: Agamben explicitly invokes Foucault’s panopticon and archaeology as resources for his paradigmatic method.
substantive_relations.note: Own interview pp. 610 and 613 read. Acknowledged methodological resource, not an assertion that Foucault endorsed Agamben or that their projects coincide.
